gaps: The plan omits the invite return path: a signed-out visitor must reach the invite after sign-in and onboarding, while an existing member goes straight to it. It specifies neither a durable return-path handoff nor a test, even though the authentication design carries that path in OAuth state (docs/specs/accounts.md:41; docs/specs/accounts.md:152; docs/architecture/12-auth-sessions-security.md:5).

The production plan says only the owner will use the app before all stories ship, but does not say how a publicly reachable app with Google sign-in will prevent other people from onboarding. The owner-only release boundary is binding (docs/decisions/0009-launch-after-full-mvp.md:17; docs/product/BRIEF.md:53).

The setup handoff does not explain how OWNER_GOOGLE_ACCOUNT_ID is bootstrapped: the owner is meant to read it from their profile after signing in, while deployment configuration is validated at API startup. It also leaves the required production configuration and who verifies each value out of the promised checklist (docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:24; docs/architecture/10-system-overview.md:77).

The account task has no explicit transaction and concurrency contract for simultaneous onboarding submissions, conversion of a pending session, and removal of pending identity. A unique Google ID alone does not describe the response or cleanup when two requests race (docs/architecture/11-data-model.md:13; docs/architecture/12-auth-sessions-security.md:14; plans/roadmap.json:11).

The plan names session expiry but does not cover the specified 30-day idle refresh, 401 behavior, or how a local session becomes invalid after Google access is revoked. Its proposed expiry test could pass without proving those behaviors (docs/architecture/12-auth-sessions-security.md:20; docs/specs/accounts.md:37).

The plan says a material notice forces re-acceptance but does not define how a version is published or how the API blocks every member action until acceptance. The specified boundary is server enforced and forbids new data use before consent (docs/specs/accounts.md:79; docs/specs/accounts.md:81; docs/architecture/00-handoff-guide.md:32).

The privacy-notice handoff does not explicitly require the first version to state that data is stored in Singapore and to match the provider's backup retention, or require approval of that exact published text before onboarding is enabled (docs/decisions/0013-hosting-render-cloudflare.md:30; docs/specs/accounts.md:75; docs/specs/accounts.md:79).

The foundation and web tasks omit explicit proof for the binding web CSP, API HSTS, production exclusion of the test sign-in route, dependency audit, and committed OpenAPI diff check. The generic 'CI runs every check' line does not identify which task installs these gates (docs/architecture/12-auth-sessions-security.md:38; docs/architecture/12-auth-sessions-security.md:76; docs/architecture/12-auth-sessions-security.md:70; docs/architecture/10-system-overview.md:64).
contradictions: The plan requires every CWF-1 criterion to have an automated test before this story is done, yet CWF-1 includes direct circle, card, and search enforcement and visibility outcomes while those capabilities are scheduled in later stories. The plan names no current replacement authority or later proof gate for these criteria, so its done condition cannot pass as written (plans/roadmap.json:12; plans/roadmap.json:18; plans/roadmap.json:28; docs/specs/accounts.md:88).

The plan calls for a Render blueprint, while the accepted MVP deviation explicitly specifies Render and Cloudflare configuration in their dashboards with no infrastructure as code. A blueprint changes that deployment contract without an accepted replacement decision (docs/architecture/90-constitution-deviations.md:11; docs/decisions/0013-hosting-render-cloudflare.md:36).
resolutions: The signed OAuth state carries a return path through Google and onboarding and is tested in CWF-1; the invite behaviour itself is roadmap CWF-2's criterion.
Owner-only production is enforced by a LAUNCH_OPEN switch and email allowlist that stores nothing for refused sign-ins (accepted decision 0016), tested and checked in production.
The API boots without the owner ID; the owner reads it from the profile and sets it before any circle exists; the deployment runbook lists every setting, who supplies it and how it is checked.

Onboarding submission is one transaction creating member and consent, removing the pending identity and upgrading the session; a concurrent duplicate gets a conflict and continues as the existing member.
30-day idle expiry refreshed on use, 401 then sign-in screen; Google tokens are not kept, so revocation takes effect at expiry or next sign-in, which satisfies the spec's illustrative example.
Notice versions are published by migration; a material-change version blocks every member route except notice read/accept and sign-out with a notice-acceptance-required error until accepted.
Version 1 states Singapore storage and the 3-day point-in-time and 7-day backup periods and is published only after the owner approves the exact text.

The foundation task installs HSTS/Helmet, the production dependency audit and the OpenAPI diff; the accounts task keeps the test route out of production builds; the web task serves the CSP; each has a named check in the verify plan.

Done now means proven on the surfaces this story builds, via one shared member-only guard and own-profile-only email/ID; CWF-2 to CWF-4 re-prove the circle, card and search parts through the same checks.
Replaced the Render blueprint with dashboard configuration recorded in a deployment runbook, as decision 0014 requires.

artifact_delta.cold:
through the certified `openid-client` library rather than Passport, because
  sessions are server-side and not JWTs; WhatsApp numbers are validated and
  normalised to E.164 with `libphonenumber-js`. Pending sign-ins, per-device
  sessions, members, consents and notice versions follow the data model; a
  notice version flagged as a material change forces re-acceptance; the daily
  cleanup runs in-process; the test sign-in route exists only in tests.
- Web: TanStack Router and Query, Tailwind and shadcn/ui, an orval client
  generated from the OpenAPI file, and a service worker that caches only the
  app shell; screens for sign-in, onboarding, profile, re-acceptance and
  session expiry, designed mobile-first.
- Deployment: a Render blueprint for the API and database in Singapore with
  migrations as the pre-deploy step, Cloudflare Pages for the web app, DNS for
  the domain and its API subdomain, and a Google sign-in client in production
  status.
artifact_delta.final:
through `openid-client`, and E.164 WhatsApp numbers through
  `libphonenumber-js`. The signed state carries a return path through Google
  and onboarding, which CWF-2 uses for invite links. The pre-launch gate
  refuses non-listed emails before anything is stored. Onboarding submission is
  one transaction that creates the member and consent, removes the pending
  identity and upgrades the session; a concurrent duplicate gets a conflict and
  the web app continues as the existing member. Sessions have a 30-day idle
  expiry refreshed on use; an expired or unknown session gets 401 and the
  sign-in screen. Google tokens are not kept, so revoking Google access takes
  effect when the session expires or at the next sign-in.
- One shared guard lets only completed members reach member routes, and a
  member's own-profile response is the only one carrying email and Google
  account ID; later stories' routes reuse both.
- Privacy notice versions are published by a database migration. When the
  latest version is flagged as a material change, every member route except
  reading and accepting the notice and signing out returns a
  notice-acceptance-required error until the member accepts. Version 1 states
  that data is stored in Singapore and the backup periods (3-day point-in-time
  restore, 7-day daily backups), and is published only after you approve it.
- Owner ID bootstrap: the API boots without the owner ID; you sign in, copy
  your ID from the profile and set it before any circle exists.
- Web: TanStack Router and Query, Tailwind and shadcn/ui, an orval client from
  the OpenAPI file, a service worker caching only the app shell, and a strict
  Content-Security-Policy served by Cloudflare Pages; screens for sign-in,
  not-open-yet, onboarding, profile, re-acceptance and session expiry, designed
  mobile-first.
- Deployment: Render and Cloudflare configured in their dashboards (no
  infrastructure-as-code), recorded in a deployment runbook that lists every
  setting, who supplies it and how it is checked; API and database in
  Singapore with migrations run before each deploy; DNS for the domain and its
  API subdomain; Google sign-in client in production status.
